request.text: I want to walk outside at 7 tomorrow morning. Check the forecast and, independently, set a 7:00 reminder to check my blood sugar. Once the forecast result is available, tell me whether to plan the outdoor walk or switch to an indoor routine.

responsibilities.outcome: Obtain the forecast relevant to an outdoor walk at 7:00 tomorrow morning.
Independently create a reminder for 7:00 tomorrow morning to check the user's blood sugar.
After the forecast result becomes available, advise whether to plan the outdoor walk or use an indoor routine based on that result.

semantic_facts: All three responsibilities should remain independently traceable: r1 obtains the specified forecast, r2 creates the 7:00 blood-sugar reminder, and r3 provides a weather-grounded outdoor-versus-indoor recommendation.
The weather lookup and reminder creation are independent and may proceed concurrently; r3 must remain ordered after trusted weather Evidence for r1 becomes available.
The eventual recommendation should concern the exercise setting and should not reinterpret or medically manage the user's blood-sugar routine.
forbidden_claims: The assistant states actual forecast conditions or chooses outdoor versus indoor activity before trusted weather Evidence exists.
The assistant claims the blood-sugar reminder has been created before trusted execution Evidence exists.
The assistant changes blood-sugar monitoring instructions or gives unsupported medical treatment advice.
The dependency of r3 on r1 is incorrectly applied to r2, delaying or dropping the independent reminder.

target.claim_boundary: assistant-authored candidate oracle; not independently reviewed

negative_hypotheses: A three-responsibility mixture loses one scope or merges a conditional response into an unrelated stateful effect.
A dependency applying only to the evidence-grounded response incorrectly blocks independent reminder execution.
The planner fabricates a weather-dependent recommendation instead of preserving the post-Evidence boundary.
